A three-finger long press starts a recording, and the same press again sends it. ScrawlKit stays inert on a device that is not paired: no gesture recognizers, overlay window, network calls, files or background
On a paired device, the trigger turns off iOS's three-finger text-editing gestures in the app. Otherwise the same press opens the Undo · Cut · Copy · Redo bar in a focused text field.

While recording, a slim strip sits on the right edge. Drag its dot to move it up, down or to the left edge, and it remembers the place.
From top to bottom it holds the recording dot, Draw, Discard and Send. Hold the dot to see the elapsed time.
Draw turns red strokes on or off. Discard gives a few seconds to Undo.
The strip moves like liquid, the Liquid morph variant of
. It pours into the tapped button to become a status circle.
It buds a bubble off on a neck, such as "Sent to …", "Discarded · Undo" or "Mac didn't answer · Share".
On iOS 26 the strip is Liquid Glass. Reduce Motion cross-fades instead.
Drawn strokes are smooth and fade on their own.
Every coalesced touch is a sample at the touch's own timestamp, so a busy main thread does not make strokes jagged.
A one-euro filter, with one cutoff from the 2D speed, takes out jitter as samples come in. A centered smoothing takes out the rest behind the tip without lag.
The line is a centripetal Catmull-Rom curve with tapered ends.
It is 4.6 pt wide when drawn slowly and down to 55% when fast. Width comes from speed, never pressure, like the Mac's ink.
Finished stretches go into layers that never change, so each touch redraws only the live tip.
The tip runs ahead through iOS's predicted touches. Predicted points are dropped on the next touch and never recorded.
A stroke fades out over 300 ms, eased out, 1.5 s after the pen last lifted.
A pen that comes down again before then holds every stroke on screen, so a circle and then an arrow fade together.
The timeline gets the smoothed, unpredicted points, plus
on each stroke that began to fade during the recording.
On keyframes the Mac draws a stroke from when it began until 1.2 s after it ended, or with the rest of its mark.
Neither capture method draws touches on screen.
Each touch goes on the timeline with its position, phase and the label of the element under it. The Mac draws taps and swipes from it.

The app can say which screen it is on and add its own keys and values, so the agent does not guess from pixels. ScrawlKit sends only what the app passes in, plus its bundle ID, name, version and build.

SettingsView().scrawlScreen("Settings › Experimental")   // while visible; restores the previous on disappear
SessionView().scrawlContext("session", session.id)       // follows the value; nil leaves it to enclosing views
Scrawl.screen("Onboarding")                              // or set either one directly (nil clears)
Scrawl.context("server", "studio")
The most recently appeared screen that is still visible wins, so pushed screens, sheets and tabs work.

ScrawlKit writes a timeline JSON beside each movie, and the bundle keeps it as
. Times are seconds from the start, and points are in the touch window's points.

fields.name: app
fields.description: `CFBundleDisplayName`, else `CFBundleName`, else the bundle ID. Ingest matches it to a session title when `session` is missing.

fields.name: bundleId
fields.description: The host app's bundle identifier.

fields.name: version
fields.description: The build, from `CFBundleVersion`.

fields.name: shortVersion
fields.description: The marketing version, from `CFBundleShortVersionString`.

fields.name: device
fields.description: The device's user-visible name.

fields.name: system
fields.description: OS name and version, such as `iOS 18.2`.

fields.name: screen
fields.description: The touch window's size in points and its display scale.

fields.name: scale
fields.description: The Mac reads a missing scale as `1`.

fields.name: recordedAt
fields.description: ISO 8601 start time. Ingest uses it as the key that joins copies of one upload.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Length in seconds. The Mac takes the length from the movie instead.

fields.name: session
fields.description: The paired destination from the setup link. Omitted when the link named none. It is the recorded destination.

fields.name: capture
fields.description: The capture method.

fields.name: audio
fields.description: `false` when the microphone was denied or narration was off.

fields.name: markers
fields.description: Marker times. Each becomes a flag.

fields.name: events
fields.description: `Scrawl.event` calls. Each lands in `summary.md` under the keyframe on screen at `t`.

fields.name: touches
fields.description: One entry per touch change. `phase` is `down`, `move`, `up`, `cancel` or `other`, and moves are logged at most 30 times a second.

fields.name: strokes
fields.description: Smoothed strokes. Each point is `[x, y, t]`, and `fadeAt` is when the stroke began to fade.

fields.name: context
fields.description: App values when the recording started.

fields.name: contextChanges
fields.description: Later changes. A `null` value means the key was cleared.

fields.name: screens
fields.description: Screen changes. The first is at `0` when the app named a screen before recording, and a `null` name means none.

Uploads are file uploads on a background

The session is made again each time the app is configured, and it picks up uploads still in flight from an earlier launch.
A 401 or 403 (a revoked link), a 413 (too large) and any other 4xx except 408 and 429 are permanent. The entry stays on disk, marked failed, with Share.

Anything else, such as no network, a timeout, 408, 429 or a 5xx, is retried after 15 s, doubling to 30 min. A retry also starts when the network comes back, the app comes to the front, or it launches.
An entry never uploads twice at once. The server dedupes on person and
, so a resend after a lost reply is safe.
Opening a new setup link retries the entries that failed with the old one.
While the upload runs on a working network, the strip stays up as a small status circle with a progress ring and says "Sending…". Touches on it reach the app.
. After 30 s with no bytes going out, the strip says "Still sending…", never "Queued".
When the upload lands, the strip says "Sent to …" with a success haptic. If the strip is gone by then, it comes back briefly with "Sent to …" as soon as the app is in front.

"Queued · sends when online" shows only for no network or a failed try that waits to retry, with a success haptic. It leaves after a few seconds, and a retry that starts while it is up turns it back to "Sending…".
A permanent failure says "Scrawl link expired · Ask Kit for a new one", "Too large to send" or "Couldn't send", with Share. Share shares copies of the recording and leaves the entry queued.
check at the start of a recording also goes to the HTTPS endpoint. A 401 there shows "Scrawl link expired" beside the strip.
The recording carries on and stays in the outbox, marked failed, until the link is renewed.
The endpoint rejects bodies over 95 MB, so HTTPS recordings are smaller and capped. The rows compare the Mac path with the two HTTPS paths.

3 Mbps at 880×1912 and 30 fps is about 0.06 bits per pixel. That is enough for app UI, which is mostly static between scrolls and transitions. The 25 MB of headroom covers an encoder that overshoots its average.

Ten seconds before the cap, the strip shows "Length limit · Sending in 10 s" with a warning haptic, then sends. A payload still over the limit is never uploaded: it is marked "Too large to send" and kept for Share.
An app with an app delegate can forward background session events, so iOS can relaunch a killed app to finish reporting uploads. Without this, finished uploads are picked up at the next launch.
